This is first application filed by the applicant under Section 439 of the Cr.P.C. for grant of regular bail relating to FIR/Crime No.70/2023 dated16.02.2023 registered at Police Station Chhepabad District Harda for the offence punishable under Sections 363, 366, 376(2)(n) of IPC and Section 5/6 of POCSO Act.
2. Leaned counsel for the applicant contends that the applicant is aged about 20 years and he is in custody since 18.03.2023.
learned counsel contends that the prosecutrix was aged about 17 years 9 moths and 11 days at the time of commission of offence.

It is alleged that as the prosecutix got Nandram Alias Nandu vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 16 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/189239763/
1 pregnant, an FIR was lodged against the applicant.

sentences.text: However the statement of the prosecutrix recorded under Section 164 of Cr.P.C. reveals that prosecutrix on her own volition, indulge in sexual intercourse with the present applicant and they also entered into wedlock.
Therefore, considering the totality of circumstances, the applicant deserves to be enlarged on bail.
3. Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent has opposed the prayer and submitted that considering the serious allegations against the applicant, the application deserves to be dismissed.

4. Heard the submissions and perused the case diary.
5.
A perusal of the case diary it reflects that the applicant who himself is aged about 20 years, is in custody since 18/03/2023.
The criminal antecedents of the applicant is unblemished.
The statement of the prosecutrix recorded under Section 164 of Cr.P.C also prima facie reflect the facutm of relationship between the prosecutrix and the applicant.
6. Thus taking into considering the overall facts and circumstances of the case, this Court is of the considered view that it is a fit case to release the applicant on bail.
Therefore, without expressing any view on the merits of the case, the application is allowed.

7 . It is directed that the applicant shall be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond in a sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) with one surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court concerned for his appearance before the said Court on all such dates as may be fixed in this regard during the pendency of trial.

8. It is further directed that the applicant shall comply with the provisions of Section 437(3) of the Cr.P.C.
9.
Accordingly, M.Cr.C. stands disposed of.
